commands.name: data-analysis

commands.name: hypothesis-generation

commands.name: design

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings up to many, some of them uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. Pass --max-findings <n> to report up to n findings, or --max-findings all for every finding. The choice stays until you pass --max-findings default. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

commands.name: simplify

Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx) or Word templates (.dotx). Triggers include: any mention of Microsoft Word Documents, such as 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', 'microsoft doc'. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a deliverable as a Word or .docx file (to download, email or print), use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or coding unrelated to document generation. (claude.ai sync)

commands.name: google-workspace
commands.description: Read this before the first Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides connector call whenever the task creates or changes a Google file. Use this skill whenever the user wants to create or change a Google Doc, Sheet or Slides file in their Google Drive. Triggers include: a request that names Google Docs, Sheets, Slides or Drive and asks to make, edit, format, copy or rename a file; a docs.google.com link with a request to change that file, even a one-line fix or suggested edits; and any follow-up change to a Google file from earlier in the chat, even "change it" or "add a tab". Includes helper scripts for document positions, cell ranges and slide layout. However, if the user asks for a doc, deck or spreadsheet without naming Google, or gives a Google file only as source material for something new, use Claude's own output type instead. commands.name: xlsx

This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. content.content:
1	# Planning: The Forgetting Tax
2	
3	Written before any training run. The analysis plan in "Statistical Analysis Plan" is the
4	pre-registration; deviations are logged at the bottom.
5	
6	## Motivation & Novelty Assessment
7	
8	### Why This Research Matters
9	Instruction-tuned LLMs are updated sequentially in practice (new tasks, new customers, new data).
10	Each update silently erodes earlier skills. Practitioners budget for this with a single number
11	("average forgetting"), but if erosion has a characteristic *shape* over time and differs by *kind of
12	skill*, then replay budgets, evaluation schedules and task ordering can be planned far better.
13	
14	### Gap in Existing Work
15	Note: the resource-finding stage was skipped for this run (`.neurico/pipeline_state.json` says
16	`"skipped": true`), so there is no `literature_review.md`, `papers/` or `code/`. The following is from
17	my own knowledge of the literature, not from a fresh review.
18	- Continual instruction-tuning benchmarks (TRACE, Wang et al. 2023; CITB, Zhang et al. 2023;
19	  Luo et al. 2023 "An Empirical Study of Catastrophic Forgetting in LLMs during Continual
20	  Fine-tuning"; Scialom et al. 2022) report *end-of-stream* averages (average accuracy, backward
21	  transfer). They rarely report the forgetting *trajectory* at sub-task resolution, and do not fit
22	  functional forms to it.
23	- Task order is usually fixed (one or two orders), so "which task type forgets more" is confounded
24	  with "which task came first".
25	- Different tasks are scored with different metrics, so cross-domain "rate" comparisons depend on an
26	  unstated normalisation.
27	
28	### Our Novel Contribution
29	1. Dense forgetting trajectories (evaluation every 50 gradient steps) so decay *shape* can be tested
30	   by model comparison (linear vs exponential vs power law).
31	2. A Williams (balanced Latin-square) order design: every task appears at every position once and
32	   follows every other task once, which de-confounds task domain from learning position.
33	3. Rate comparison between reasoning and pattern-matching tasks under three explicit normalisations,
34	   including a metric-free one (held-out loss).
35	
36	### Experiment Justification
37	- **Exp 1 (main, sequential LoRA, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, 6 orders x 2 seeds):** provides the
38	  trajectories all three sub-hypotheses are tested on.
39	- **Exp 2 (baselines: zero-shot and joint multi-task training):** zero-shot is the floor needed to
40	  define "learned gain"; joint training shows whether drops are forgetting or mere capacity limits.
41	- **Exp 3 (replication on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, 6 orders):** are conclusions model-specific?
42	- **Exp 4 (ablation: full fine-tuning instead of LoRA, 6 orders):** are conclusions specific to the
43	  low-rank adapter?
44	
45	## Research Question
46	During sequential instruction tuning on six tasks, (H1) does retained performance on a previously
47	learned task decay as a power law in the amount of subsequent training, rather than linearly
48	("uniform degradation") or exponentially? (H2) Do reasoning tasks (math, logic) lose performance
49	3-5x faster than pattern-matching tasks (translation, summarisation)? (H3) Are early-learned tasks
50	forgotten disproportionately, i.e. more than their longer exposure to interference explains?
51	
52	## Hypothesis Decomposition
53	- **H1 (shape).** IV: interfering gradient steps `t` since the task's own stage ended (0..1250).
54	  DV: retention `R(t)`. Candidates: linear `1-at` (1 param), exponential `exp(-t/tau)` (1),
55	  power law `(1+t/tau)^-b` (2), exponential-to-asymptote `c+(1-c)exp(-t/tau)` (2, a fair
56	  2-parameter competitor). Supported if the power law has the lowest AICc in a clear majority of
57	  task-level mean curves AND beats the 2-parameter exponential.
58	- **H2 (domain).** IV: task category. DV: forgetting rate. Supported if the reasoning/pattern ratio
59	  of mean forgetting has a bootstrap 95% CI that lies inside or overlaps [3, 5] and excludes 1,
60	  consistently across normalisations. A ratio >1 but well outside [3,5] is "direction right,
61	  magnitude wrong".
62	- **H3 (position).** IV: serial position 1..6. Final retention vs position is necessarily
63	  confounded with lag (earlier = more interference), so the "disproportionate" claim is tested by
64	  (a) forgetting at a *fixed* lag (after exactly one subsequent task) as a function of position, and
65	  (b) a regression of retention on log(1+lag), position and task with run-clustered errors.
66	  Supported if position has a negative effect on retention beyond lag.
67	
68	## Proposed Methodology
69	### Approach
70	Real sequential fine-tuning of open instruction-tuned LLMs on local GPUs (4x RTX A6000). API models
71	cannot be continually fine-tuned with trajectory access, so no API models are used (and
72	`OPENROUTER_KEY` is not set in this environment).
73	
74	### Tasks (2000 train / 200 test each; `src/prep_data.py`)
75	| Task | Category | Source | Metric |
76	|---|---|---|---|
77	| gsm8k | reasoning | GSM8K, worked solution + answer | exact-match accuracy |
78	| arith | reasoning | synthetic 3-step integer arithmetic | exact-match accuracy |
79	| logic | reasoning | ProofWriter OWA, depth 1-3, 3-way | accuracy |
80	| mt | pattern | WMT16 en->de (newstest2015 train / 2016 test) | chrF |
81	| summ | pattern | SAMSum | ROUGE-L F1 |
82	| emotion | pattern | dair-ai/emotion, 6-way | accuracy |
83	
84	`emotion` is included so that the pattern category has an accuracy-scored task; otherwise category
85	would be perfectly confounded with metric type. The reasoning/pattern assignment is a judgment call;

# Planning: The Forgetting Tax

Written before any training run. The analysis plan in "Statistical Analysis Plan" is the
pre-registration; deviations are logged at the bottom.

## Motivation & Novelty Assessment

### Why This Research Matters
Instruction-tuned LLMs are updated sequentially in practice (new tasks, new customers, new data).
Each update silently erodes earlier skills. Practitioners budget for this with a single number
("average forgetting"), but if erosion has a characteristic *shape* over time and differs by *kind of
skill*, then replay budgets, evaluation schedules and task ordering can be planned far better.

### Gap in Existing Work
Note: the resource-finding stage was skipped for this run (`.neurico/pipeline_state.json` says
`"skipped": true`), so there is no `literature_review.md`, `papers/` or `code/`. The following is from
my own knowledge of the literature, not from a fresh review.
- Continual instruction-tuning benchmarks (TRACE, Wang et al. 2023; CITB, Zhang et al. 2023;
  Luo et al. 2023 "An Empirical Study of Catastrophic Forgetting in LLMs during Continual
  Fine-tuning"; Scialom et al. 2022) report *end-of-stream* averages (average accuracy, backward
  transfer). They rarely report the forgetting *trajectory* at sub-task resolution, and do not fit
  functional forms to it.
- Task order is usually fixed (one or two orders), so "which task type forgets more" is confounded
  with "which task came first".
- Different tasks are scored with different metrics, so cross-domain "rate" comparisons depend on an
  unstated normalisation.

### Our Novel Contribution
1. Dense forgetting trajectories (evaluation every 50 gradient steps) so decay *shape* can be tested
   by model comparison (linear vs exponential vs power law).
2. A Williams (balanced Latin-square) order design: every task appears at every position once and
   follows every other task once, which de-confounds task domain from learning position.
3. Rate comparison between reasoning and pattern-matching tasks under three explicit normalisations,
   including a metric-free one (held-out loss).

### Experiment Justification
- **Exp 1 (main, sequential LoRA, Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, 6 orders x 2 seeds):** provides the
  trajectories all three sub-hypotheses are tested on.
- **Exp 2 (baselines: zero-shot and joint multi-task training):** zero-shot is the floor needed to
  define "learned gain"; joint training shows whether drops are forgetting or mere capacity limits.
- **Exp 3 (replication on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, 6 orders):** are conclusions model-specific?
- **Exp 4 (ablation: full fine-tuning instead of LoRA, 6 orders):** are conclusions specific to the
  low-rank adapter?

## Research Question
During sequential instruction tuning on six tasks, (H1) does retained performance on a previously
learned task decay as a power law in the amount of subsequent training, rather than linearly
("uniform degradation") or exponentially? (H2) Do reasoning tasks (math, logic) lose performance
3-5x faster than pattern-matching tasks (translation, summarisation)? (H3) Are early-learned tasks
forgotten disproportionately, i.e. more than their longer exposure to interference explains?

## Hypothesis Decomposition
- **H1 (shape).** IV: interfering gradient steps `t` since the task's own stage ended (0..1250).
  DV: retention `R(t)`. Candidates: linear `1-at` (1 param), exponential `exp(-t/tau)` (1),
  power law `(1+t/tau)^-b` (2), exponential-to-asymptote `c+(1-c)exp(-t/tau)` (2, a fair
  2-parameter competitor). Supported if the power law has the lowest AICc in a clear majority of
  task-level mean curves AND beats the 2-parameter exponential.
- **H2 (domain).** IV: task category. DV: forgetting rate. Supported if the reasoning/pattern ratio
  of mean forgetting has a bootstrap 95% CI that lies inside or overlaps [3, 5] and excludes 1,
  consistently across normalisations. A ratio >1 but well outside [3,5] is "direction right,
  magnitude wrong".
- **H3 (position).** IV: serial position 1..6. Final retention vs position is necessarily
  confounded with lag (earlier = more interference), so the "disproportionate" claim is tested by
  (a) forgetting at a *fixed* lag (after exactly one subsequent task) as a function of position, and
  (b) a regression of retention on log(1+lag), position and task with run-clustered errors.
  Supported if position has a negative effect on retention beyond lag.

## Proposed Methodology
### Approach
Real sequential fine-tuning of open instruction-tuned LLMs on local GPUs (4x RTX A6000). API models
cannot be continually fine-tuned with trajectory access, so no API models are used (and
`OPENROUTER_KEY` is not set in this environment).

### Tasks (2000 train / 200 test each; `src/prep_data.py`)
| Task | Category | Source | Metric |
|---|---|---|---|
| gsm8k | reasoning | GSM8K, worked solution + answer | exact-match accuracy |
| arith | reasoning | synthetic 3-step integer arithmetic | exact-match accuracy |
| logic | reasoning | ProofWriter OWA, depth 1-3, 3-way | accuracy |
| mt | pattern | WMT16 en->de (newstest2015 train / 2016 test) | chrF |
| summ | pattern | SAMSum | ROUGE-L F1 |
| emotion | pattern | dair-ai/emotion, 6-way | accuracy |

`emotion` is included so that the pattern category has an accuracy-scored task; otherwise category
would be perfectly confounded with metric type. The reasoning/pattern assignment is a judgment call;
results are also reported per task.

### Experimental Steps
1. Zero-shot evaluation of the base model on all six test sets.
2. Sequential training: for each order, train task 1 for 250 steps (batch 16 = 2 epochs), then task
   2, ... with a single LoRA adapter carried through (r=16, alpha=32, all attention+MLP projections,
   lr 2e-4, AdamW, **constant** LR after a 10-step warm-up per stage so that interference per step is
   not modulated by a schedule). No replay, no regularisation (naive SeqFT, the standard lower bound).
3. Every 50 steps: held-out per-token loss on all six test sets and greedy-decoded task metrics.
4. Orders: 6-order Williams design; seed 2 uses a randomly relabelled Williams square.
5. Joint baseline: 1500 steps on the mixture of all six tasks.
6. Replication on Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and full-fine-tuning ablation (lr 1e-5), 6 orders each.

### Baselines
Zero-shot base model (floor), joint multi-task training (upper bound), each task's own
end-of-stage performance (per-trajectory reference).

### Evaluation Metrics
For task i in a run, with `m0` zero-shot score, `m*` the score at the end of its own stage, `m(t)`
after `t` further steps:
- **Gain-normalised retention** `R_gain = (m(t)-m0)/(m*-m0)` (fraction of learned gain kept; only
  defined where `m*-m0` is non-trivial; trajectories with gain < 0.05 are excluded and counted).
- **Relative retention** `R_rel = m(t)/m*`.
- **Loss-based retention** `R_loss = (L0-L(t))/(L0-L*)` using held-out per-token NLL: metric-free and
  comparable across tasks. This is the primary measure for H1 because it is continuous.
- Forgetting at lag k = `1 - R` after k subsequent tasks; standard final-forgetting / BWT as well.

### Statistical Analysis Plan
- H1: non-linear least squares on task-level mean curves and on individual trajectories; AICc and
  win counts; residual plots. alpha = 0.05 throughout.
- H2: ratio of category means of forgetting (averaged over lags 1-5, each task weighted equally),
  cluster bootstrap over runs (10,000 resamples), under all three normalisations; plus
  per-task table so the reader can see whether one task drives the category effect.
- H3: fixed-lag comparison with Spearman correlation and the regression above (cluster-robust by
  run); position x lag is only partially crossed, stated as a limitation.
- Multiple comparisons: Holm correction across the three normalisations within each hypothesis.
- No conclusions from individual 200-example test deltas < ~7 points (binomial SE ~3.5 points).

## Expected Outcomes
Supporting: power law wins AICc; ratio CI inside [3,5]; negative position effect beyond lag.
Refuting: exponential/linear fit as well or better; ratio near 1, reversed, or dominated by a single
task; no position effect once lag is controlled.

## Timeline and Milestones
Setup+data 30 min (done) | implementation + smoke test 40 min | main runs ~60-90 min on 4 GPUs |
replication + ablation ~60 min | analysis 45 min | report 30 min.

## Potential Challenges
- Small learned gain on tasks the base model already does well (mt, gsm8k) makes `R_gain` noisy ->
  loss-based retention is primary; exclusions are counted and reported.
- /data has ~9 GB free: no checkpoints are saved; only JSON results.
- 200 test items per task: coarse for accuracy; mitigated by 12 runs and loss-based measure.

## Success Criteria
All planned runs complete, each sub-hypothesis receives a clear supported / not supported /
inconclusive verdict with uncertainty, and negative results are reported as such.

## Deviations from plan
(appended during execution)
- (before any run, after the smoke test) Evaluation cadence changed from "loss and generation every
  50 steps" to "held-out loss every 25 steps, generation metrics every 125 steps (mid-stage and
  end-of-stage)". Reason: generation costs ~45 s per evaluation point; loss costs ~3 s. H1 (shape)
  therefore rests on the loss trajectories (51 points per lag axis) with the generation metrics as a
  coarser (11-point) check.
- (before any run) Full-fine-tuning ablation learning rate set to 2e-5 instead of 1e-5 so that 250
  steps are enough to learn each task.
- (before any run) Generation budgets for gsm8k/arith raised to 320/160 tokens: the smoke test showed
  the verbose zero-shot answers for arith were truncated at 48 tokens before the final answer, which
  would have understated the zero-shot floor.
- The GPUs are shared with other jobs that started during setup; runs are packed onto whichever
  GPUs have free memory, with automatic retry.
- (during execution, 16:25) The full-fine-tuning ablation (Exp 4) was cancelled before any of its runs
  started. Reason: the four GPUs turned out to be shared with other jobs holding ~44 GB each; LoRA runs
  that take ~10 min on a free GPU took ~100 min, and full fine-tuning needs ~3x the memory. No
  full-FT data exists, so this is a scope cut, not a selective omission.
- (during execution) Two main runs and the Qwen joint baseline died with CUDA out-of-memory when a
  neighbouring job grew; they were restarted from scratch (same seed/config). The run script was
  changed to wait for memory instead of exiting. Because micro-batching with gradient accumulation
  keeps the objective identical, runs differ only in floating-point summation order.

"""Sequential (continual) instruction tuning with dense forgetting evaluation.

One invocation = one run (one task order, one seed, one model). After every
`eval_every` optimizer steps all six test sets are evaluated with (a) held-out
per-token loss on the reference target and (b) greedy-decoded task metrics.
Results are appended to a JSONL file after each evaluation, so a crashed run
still leaves usable data. No model checkpoints are written (disk is scarce).

Usage:
  python src/run_continual.py --order gsm8k,arith,logic,mt,summ,emotion --seed 0 --tag main
  python src/run_continual.py --joint --seed 0 --tag joint
"""
import argparse
import gc
import json
import math
import os
import random
import re
import sys
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
from rouge_score import rouge_scorer
from sacrebleu.metrics import CHRF
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

TASKS = ["gsm8k", "arith", "logic", "mt", "summ", "emotion"]
# budgets are generous enough that verbose zero-shot answers are not cut off before the final answer
MAX_NEW = {"gsm8k": 320, "arith": 160, "logic": 4, "mt": 96, "summ": 64, "emotion": 4}
DATA = "datasets/processed"
MAX_LEN = 640  # tokens; longer training sequences are truncated (rare, see log)


def set_seed(seed):
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)


def load_task(task, split):
    with open(f"{DATA}/{task}_{split}.jsonl") as f:
        return [json.loads(line) for line in f]


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- scoring
_chrf = CHRF()
_rouge = rouge_scorer.RougeScorer(["rougeL"], use_stemmer=True)


def extract_number(text):
    """Final numeric answer: prefer the 'Answer: x' line, else the last number in the text."""
    m = re.findall(r"Answer:\s*\$?\s*(-?[\d,]*\.?\d+)", text)
    if not m:
        m = re.findall(r"-?[\d,]*\.?\d+", text)
    if not m:
        return None
    try:
        return float(m[-1].replace(",", ""))
    except ValueError:
        return None


def score(task, pred, ex):
    """Per-example score in [0, 1]."""
    if task in ("gsm8k", "arith"):
        v = extract_number(pred)
        return float(v is not None and abs(v - float(ex["answer"])) < 1e-4)
    if task in ("logic", "emotion"):
        w = re.findall(r"[a-z]+", pred.lower())
        return float(bool(w) and w[0] == ex["answer"].lower())
    if task == "mt":
        return _chrf.sentence_score(pred.strip(), [ex["answer"]]).score / 100.0
    if task == "summ":
        return _rouge.score(ex["answer"], pred.strip())["rougeL"].fmeasure
    raise ValueError(task)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- encoding
def encode_prompt(tok, prompt):
    return tok.apply_chat_template([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}], tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)


def build_supervised(tok, rows):
    """Token ids + labels with the prompt masked out (loss on the assistant answer only)."""
    out, n_trunc = [], 0
    for r in rows:
        p = tok(encode_prompt(tok, r["prompt"]), add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
        t = tok(r["target"] + tok.eos_token, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
        ids, lab = (p + t), ([-100] * len(p) + t)
        if len(ids) > MAX_LEN:
            n_trunc += 1
            ids, lab = ids[:MAX_LEN], lab[:MAX_LEN]
        out.append((ids, lab))
    return out, n_trunc


def collate(batch, pad_id, device):
    n = max(len(i) for i, _ in batch)
    ids = torch.full((len(batch), n), pad_id, dtype=torch.long)
    lab = torch.full((len(batch), n), -100, dtype=torch.long)
    att = torch.zeros((len(batch), n), dtype=torch.long)
    for k, (i, l) in enumerate(batch):
        ids[k, :len(i)], lab[k, :len(l)], att[k, :len(i)] = torch.tensor(i), torch.tensor(l), 1
    return ids.to(device), att.to(device), lab.to(device)


def answer_nll(model, ids, att, lab):
    """Summed cross-entropy on the supervised (answer) positions only, plus their count.

    The decoder body is run once, then the LM head is applied only to hidden states
    whose next token is supervised. This is numerically the same objective as the
    built-in `labels=` loss but avoids a batch x seq x vocab logits tensor, which
    matters because the GPUs are shared and only a few GB are free.
    """
    lm = model.get_base_model() if hasattr(model, "get_base_model") else model
    mask = lab[:, 1:] != -100
    tgt = lab[:, 1:][mask]
    with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
        hidden = lm.model(input_ids=ids, attention_mask=att).last_hidden_state[:, :-1][mask]
        # LM head + CE in chunks of answer positions to bound the vocab-sized tensors
        loss = sum(torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(lm.lm_head(hidden[c:c + 256]).float(), tgt[c:c + 256], reduction="sum")
                   for c in range(0, len(tgt), 256))
    return loss, len(tgt)


# Batch sizes are halved on a CUDA out-of-memory error and the operation is retried. Training
# uses micro-batches with gradient accumulation, so the effective batch (and the objective:
# mean NLL over all answer tokens of the 16 sequences) is unchanged when memory is tight.
BS = {"micro": 16, "loss": 16, "gen": 25}


def shrink(key):
    gc.collect()
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    if BS[key] == 1:
        # Already at the minimum: another job on the shared GPU has taken the memory. Wait for it
        # to be released rather than crash and lose the run (no checkpoints are kept).
        BS["waits"] = BS.get("waits", 0) + 1
        assert BS["waits"] < 240, f"out of GPU memory at batch size 1 for over an hour ({key})"
        print(f"OOM at {key} batch size 1: waiting 15s (wait #{BS['waits']})", flush=True)
        time.sleep(15)
        return
    BS[key] //= 2
    print(f"OOM: reducing {key} batch size to {BS[key]}", flush=True)


def train_step(model, opt, batch, pad_id, device, params):
    """One optimizer step on `batch`; returns the mean answer-token NLL."""
    n_tok = sum(sum(l != -100 for l in lab[1:]) for _, lab in batch)
    while True:
        oom = False
        try:
            opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
            total = 0.0
            for s in range(0, len(batch), BS["micro"]):
                ids, att, lab = collate(batch[s:s + BS["micro"]], pad_id, device)
                loss, _ = answer_nll(model, ids, att, lab)
                (loss / n_tok).backward()
                total += loss.item()
                del loss
        except torch.OutOfMemoryError:
            oom = True  # handled below: the traceback must be released before memory can be freed
        if not oom:
            break
        ids = att = lab = loss = None
        shrink("micro")
    torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(params, 1.0)
    opt.step()
    opt.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
    return total / n_tok


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- evaluation
@torch.no_grad()
def eval_loss(model, enc, pad_id, device):
    """Mean per-token NLL of the reference targets (token-weighted over the test set)."""
    tot, cnt = 0.0, 0
    order = sorted(range(len(enc)), key=lambda k: len(enc[k][0]))
    s = 0
    while s < len(order):
        oom = False
        try:
            ids, att, lab = collate([enc[k] for k in order[s:s + BS["loss"]]], pad_id, device)
            loss, n = answer_nll(model, ids, att, lab)
        except torch.OutOfMemoryError:
            oom = True
        if oom:
            shrink("loss")
            continue
        tot += loss.item()
        cnt += n
        s += len(ids)
    return tot / cnt


@torch.no_grad()
def eval_gen(model, tok, task, rows, device):
    """Greedy decoding; returns per-example scores and raw predictions."""
    prompts = [encode_prompt(tok, r["prompt"]) for r in rows]
    order = sorted(range(len(rows)), key=lambda k: len(prompts[k]))
    preds = [None] * len(rows)
    s = 0
    while s < len(order):
        idx = order[s:s + BS["gen"]]
        enc = tok([prompts[k] for k in idx], return_tensors="pt", padding=True, add_special_tokens=False).to(device)
        oom = False
        try:
            with torch.autocast("cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16):
                out = model.generate(**enc, max_new_tokens=MAX_NEW[task], do_sample=False,
                                     pad_token_id=tok.pad_token_id)
        except torch.OutOfMemoryError:
            oom = True
        if oom:
            enc = None
            shrink("gen")
            continue
        s += len(idx)
        txt = tok.batch_decode(out[:, enc["input_ids"].size(1):], skip_special_tokens=True)
        for k, t in zip(idx, txt):
            preds[k] = t
    return [score(task, p, r) for p, r in zip(preds, rows)], preds


def evaluate(model, tok, test, test_enc, device, do_gen=True):
    model.eval()
    res = {}
    for task in TASKS:
        res[task] = {"loss": eval_loss(model, test_enc[task], tok.pad_token_id, device)}
        if do_gen:
            sc, preds = eval_gen(model, tok, task, test[task], device)
            res[task].update(metric=float(np.mean(sc)), scores=sc, preds=preds)
    model.train()
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()  # return cached blocks: the GPUs are shared
    return res


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- main
def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--model", default="meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct")
    ap.add_argument("--order", default=",".join(TASKS))
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    ap.add_argument("--tag", default="main")
    ap.add_argument("--steps_per_task", type=int, default=250)
    ap.add_argument("--eval_every", type=int, default=25, help="held-out loss evaluation interval (steps)")
    ap.add_argument("--gen_every", type=int, default=125, help="generation-metric evaluation interval (steps)")
    ap.add_argument("--bs", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=2e-4)
    ap.add_argument("--warmup", type=int, default=10)
    ap.add_argument("--lora_r", type=int, default=16)
    ap.add_argument("--full_ft", action="store_true", help="update all weights instead of a LoRA adapter")
    ap.add_argument("--joint", action="store_true", help="multi-task baseline: train on the mixture of all tasks")
    ap.add_argument("--n_test", type=int, default=200)
    ap.add_argument("--n_train", type=int, default=2000)
    ap.add_argument("--out_dir", default="results/runs")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    order = args.order.split(",")
    assert sorted(order) == sorted(TASKS), order
    name = f"{args.tag}_{'joint' if args.joint else '-'.join(order)}_s{args.seed}"
    os.makedirs(args.out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    out_path = f"{args.out_dir}/{name}.jsonl"
    if os.path.exists(f"{args.out_dir}/.skip_{args.tag}"):
        print("skip marker present for tag", args.tag)  # lets a queued experiment group be cancelled
        return
    if os.path.exists(out_path + ".done"):
        print("already done:", name)
        return
    if os.path.exists(out_path) and time.time() - os.path.getmtime(out_path) < 900:
        print("in progress elsewhere (results file recently written):", name)
        return
    set_seed(args.seed)
    device = "cuda"

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model)
    tok.padding_side = "left"  # required for batched generation; harmless for training (attention mask)
    if tok.pad_token is None:
        tok.pad_token = "<|finetune_right_pad_id|>" if "<|finetune_right_pad_id|>" in tok.get_vocab() else tok.eos_token
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(args.model, dtype=torch.bfloat16 if not args.full_ft else torch.float32).to(device)
    if not args.full_ft:
        model = get_peft_model(model, LoraConfig(
            r=args.lora_r, lora_alpha=2 * args.lora_r, lora_dropout=0.0, task_type="CAUSAL_LM",
            target_modules=["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj", "o_proj", "gate_proj", "up_proj", "down_proj"]))
    n_train_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)

    test = {t: load_task(t, "test")[:args.n_test] for t in TASKS}
    test_enc = {t: build_supervised(tok, test[t])[0] for t in TASKS}
    train_enc = {}
    for t in TASKS:
        train_enc[t], n_trunc = build_supervised(tok, load_task(t, "train")[:args.n_train])
        print(f"{t}: {len(train_enc[t])} train examples, {n_trunc} truncated to {MAX_LEN} tokens", flush=True)

    config = dict(vars(args), name=name, order=order, n_trainable=n_train_params, torch=torch.__version__,
                  gpu=torch.cuda.get_device_name(0), started=time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"))
    f = open(out_path, "w")
    f.write(json.dumps({"config": config}) + "\n")

    def log_eval(step, stage, task_in_training):
        t0 = time.time()
        do_gen = step % args.gen_every == 0
        res = evaluate(model, tok, test, test_enc, device, do_gen=do_gen)
        rec = {"step": step, "stage": stage, "training_task": task_in_training,
               "stage_end": step % args.steps_per_task == 0, "has_gen": do_gen, "eval": res}
        # raw generations are only kept at stage boundaries to limit file size
        if do_gen and not rec["stage_end"]:
            for t in TASKS:
                res[t].pop("preds")
        f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")
        f.flush()

"""Job launcher: runs all experiment configurations over the free GPU slots.

The machine is shared with other jobs, so each worker waits until some GPU has
enough free memory before starting a run there. Finished runs (.done marker)
are skipped, failed runs (e.g. another job took the memory) are retried.

import argparse
import os
import queue
import random
import re
import subprocess
import threading
import time

TASKS = ["gsm8k", "arith", "logic", "mt", "summ", "emotion"]


def williams(n=6):
    """Williams design for even n: each item appears once per position and
    follows every other item exactly once."""
    first, lo, hi = [0], 1, n - 1
    while len(first) < n:
        first.append(lo); lo += 1
        if len(first) < n:
            first.append(hi); hi -= 1
    return [[(x + i) % n for x in first] for i in range(n)]


def orders(seed):
    """Seed 0 uses the canonical labelling, other seeds a random relabelling of tasks."""
    lab = list(TASKS)
    if seed > 0:
        random.Random(1000 + seed).shuffle(lab)
    return [",".join(lab[i] for i in row) for row in williams()]


def jobs(groups):
    out = []
    llama, qwen = "meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct", "Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct"
    if "main" in groups:
        out += [["--tag", "main", "--model", llama, "--order", o, "--seed", str(s)] for s in (0, 1) for o in orders(s)]
    if "joint" in groups:
        out += [["--tag", "joint", "--model", llama, "--joint", "--seed", str(s)] for s in (0, 1)]
        out += [["--tag", "qwenjoint", "--model", qwen, "--joint", "--seed", "0"]]
    if "qwen" in groups:
        out += [["--tag", "qwen", "--model", qwen, "--order", o, "--seed", "0"] for o in orders(0)]
    if "fullft" in groups:
        out += [["--tag", "fullft", "--model", llama, "--full_ft", "--lr", "2e-5", "--order", o, "--seed", "0"] for o in orders(0)]
    return out


LOCK = threading.Lock()


MINE = {}  # gpu index -> number of my runs currently on it


def free_gpu(need_mb):
    """Among GPUs with at least need_mb MiB free, the one running fewest of my jobs (ties: most free)."""
    out = subprocess.check_output(["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=index,memory.free", "--format=csv,noheader,nounits"], text=True)
    cand = [(MINE.get(int(l.split(",")[0]), 0), -int(l.split(",")[1]), int(l.split(",")[0]))
            for l in out.strip().splitlines() if int(l.split(",")[1]) >= need_mb]
    return min(cand)[2] if cand else None


def worker(q, wid, need_mb):
    env = dict(os.environ, HF_HUB_CACHE="/data/transformers", HF_HUB_OFFLINE="1", TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM="false",
               PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:True")

            job, tries = q.get_nowait()
        except queue.Empty:
            return
        need = need_mb * (3 if "--full_ft" in job else 1)
        # The GPUs are shared: wait until one has room. The lock + pause staggers start-ups
        # so that two workers do not both claim the same free memory.
        with LOCK:
            while (gpu := free_gpu(need)) is None:
                time.sleep(20)
            log = open(f"logs/worker_{wid}.log", "a")
            proc = subprocess.Popen(["python", "src/run_continual.py"] + job, env=dict(env, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=str(gpu)),

        MINE[gpu] -= 1
        log.close()
        print(f"{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')} worker {wid} gpu {gpu} rc={rc} tries={tries}: {' '.join(job)}", flush=True)
        if rc != 0 and tries < 8:
            q.put((job, tries + 1))

    ap.add_argument("--groups", default="main,joint,qwen,fullft")
    ap.add_argument("--match", default=".", help="regex; only jobs whose argument string matches are run")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=6)
    ap.add_argument("--need_mb", type=int, default=6000, help="free GPU memory required to start a LoRA run")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    q = queue.Queue()

    print("jobs:", q.qsize(), flush=True)
    ths = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(q, i, a.need_mb)) for i in range(a.workers)]
    [t.start() for t in ths]
    [t.join() for t in ths]
    print("ALL DONE", flush=True)

def extract_number(text):
    """Final numeric answer: prefer the 'Answer: x' line, else the last number in the text."""
    m = re.findall(r"Answer:\s*\$?\s*(-?[\d,]*\.?\d+)", text)
    if not m:
        m = re.findall(r"-?[\d,]*\.?\d+", text)
    if not m:
        return None
    try:
        return float(m[-1].replace(",", ""))
    except ValueError:
        return None

    """Per-example score in [0, 1]."""

    return [[(x + i) % n for x in first] for i in range(n)]


def orders(seed):
    """Seed 0 uses the canonical labelling, other seeds a random relabelling of tasks."""
    lab = list(TASKS)
    if seed > 0:
        random.Random(1000 + seed).shuffle(lab)
    return [",".join(lab[i] for i in row) for row in williams()]


def jobs(groups):
    out = []
    llama, qwen = "meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct", "Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct"
    if "main" in groups:
        out += [["--tag", "main", "--model", llama, "--order", o, "--seed", str(s)] for s in (0, 1) for o in orders(s)]
    if "joint" in groups:
        out += [["--tag", "joint", "--model", llama, "--joint", "--seed", str(s)] for s in (0, 1)]
        out += [["--tag", "qwenjoint", "--model", qwen, "--joint", "--seed", "0"]]
    if "qwen" in groups:
        out += [["--tag", "qwen", "--model", qwen, "--order", o, "--seed", "0"] for o in orders(0)]
    if "fullft" in groups:
        out += [["--tag", "fullft", "--model", llama, "--full_ft", "--lr", "2e-5", "--order", o, "--seed", "0"] for o in orders(0)]
    return out


LOCK = threading.Lock()


MINE = {}  # gpu index -> number of my runs currently on it


def free_gpu(need_mb):
    """Among GPUs with at least need_mb MiB free, the one running fewest of my jobs (ties: most free)."""
    out = subprocess.check_output(["nvidia-smi", "--query-gpu=index,memory.free", "--format=csv,noheader,nounits"], text=True)
    cand = [(MINE.get(int(l.split(",")[0]), 0), -int(l.split(",")[1]), int(l.split(",")[0]))
            for l in out.strip().splitlines() if int(l.split(",")[1]) >= need_mb]
    return min(cand)[2] if cand else None


def worker(q, wid, need_mb):
    env = dict(os.environ, HF_HUB_CACHE="/data/transformers", HF_HUB_OFFLINE="1", TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM="false",
               PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:True")
    while True:
        try:
            job, tries = q.get_nowait()
        except queue.Empty:
            return
        need = need_mb * (3 if "--full_ft" in job else 1)
        # The GPUs are shared: wait until one has room. The lock + pause staggers start-ups
        # so that two workers do not both claim the same free memory.
        with LOCK:
            while (gpu := free_gpu(need)) is None:
                time.sleep(20)
            log = open(f"logs/worker_{wid}.log", "a")
            proc = subprocess.Popen(["python", "src/run_continual.py"] + job, env=dict(env, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=str(gpu)),
                                    stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
            MINE[gpu] = MINE.get(gpu, 0) + 1
            time.sleep(40)
        rc = proc.wait()
        MINE[gpu] -= 1
        log.close()
        print(f"{time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')} worker {wid} gpu {gpu} rc={rc} tries={tries}: {' '.join(job)}", flush=True)
        if rc != 0 and tries < 8:
            q.put((job, tries + 1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--groups", default="main,joint,qwen,fullft")
    ap.add_argument("--match", default=".", help="regex; only jobs whose argument string matches are run")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=6)
    ap.add_argument("--need_mb", type=int, default=6000, help="free GPU memory required to start a LoRA run")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    q = queue.Queue()
    for j in jobs(a.groups.split(",")):
        if re.search(a.match, " ".join(j)):
            q.put((j, 1))
    print("jobs:", q.qsize(), flush=True)
    ths = [threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(q, i, a.need_mb)) for i in range(a.workers)]
    [t.start() for t in ths]
    [t.join() for t in ths]
    print("ALL DONE", flush=True)

content.content:
"""Analysis for the Forgetting Tax study (pre-registered in planning.md).

Reads results/runs/{tag}_*.jsonl and writes tables (results/*.csv, results/summary_{tag}.json)
and figures (figures/*.png).

  H1  shape of the retention curve: linear vs exponential vs power law
  H2  reasoning vs pattern-matching forgetting rate (ratio, three normalisations)
  H3  serial-position effect beyond lag

Usage: python src/analyze.py --tag main
"""
import argparse
import glob
import itertools
import json
import os
import warnings

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from scipy.optimize import curve_fit
from scipy.stats import spearmanr

TASKS = ["gsm8k", "arith", "logic", "mt", "summ", "emotion"]
CATEGORY = {"gsm8k": "reasoning", "arith": "reasoning", "logic": "reasoning",
            "mt": "pattern", "summ": "pattern", "emotion": "pattern"}
COLORS = {"gsm8k": "#b2182b", "arith": "#ef8a62", "logic": "#7f3b08",
          "mt": "#2166ac", "summ": "#67a9cf", "emotion": "#1b7837"}
MIN_GAIN = 0.05   # trajectories that learned less than this (metric units) are excluded from R_gain
N_BOOT = 10000
RNG = np.random.default_rng(0)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- loading
def load_runs(tag, run_dir="results/runs"):
    runs = []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(f"{run_dir}/{tag}_*.jsonl")):
        if not os.path.exists(path + ".done"):
            continue  # incomplete run
        lines = [json.loads(l) for l in open(path)]
        cfg = lines[0]["config"]
        recs = [l for l in lines if "step" in l]
        runs.append({"name": cfg["name"], "cfg": cfg, "recs": recs, "joint": cfg["joint"]})
    return runs


def trajectories(runs):
    """Long table: one row per (run, task, evaluation step at or after the task's own stage end)."""
    rows = []
    for r in runs:
        if r["joint"]:
            continue
        spt, order = r["cfg"]["steps_per_task"], r["cfg"]["order"]
        by_step = {x["step"]: x for x in r["recs"]}
        for pos, task in enumerate(order, 1):
            s_end = pos * spt
            z, star = by_step[0]["eval"][task], by_step[s_end]["eval"][task]
            for step in sorted(by_step):
                if step < s_end:
                    continue
                e = by_step[step]["eval"][task]
                row = {"run": r["name"], "seed": r["cfg"]["seed"], "task": task, "category": CATEGORY[task],
                       "position": pos, "t": step - s_end, "lag": (step - s_end) / spt,
                       "interferer": None if step == s_end else order[min((step - 1) // spt, len(order) - 1)],
                       "loss": e["loss"], "loss0": z["loss"], "loss_star": star["loss"],
                       "R_loss": (z["loss"] - e["loss"]) / (z["loss"] - star["loss"]),
                       # exploratory robustness measure (added after seeing that loss blow-ups far beyond the
                       # zero-shot level on one task dominate the unclipped mean): retention clipped to [0, 1]
                       "R_loss_clip": float(np.clip((z["loss"] - e["loss"]) / (z["loss"] - star["loss"]), 0, 1)),
                       "metric0": z["metric"], "metric_star": star["metric"], "gain": star["metric"] - z["metric"]}
                if "metric" in e:
                    row["metric"] = e["metric"]
                    row["R_rel"] = e["metric"] / star["metric"] if star["metric"] > 0 else np.nan
                    row["R_gain"] = ((e["metric"] - z["metric"]) / (star["metric"] - z["metric"])
                                     if star["metric"] - z["metric"] >= MIN_GAIN else np.nan)
                    row["abs_drop"] = star["metric"] - e["metric"]
                rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- H1: curve shape
def f_lin(x, a): return 1 - a * x
def f_exp(x, tau): return np.exp(-x / tau)
def f_pow(x, tau, b): return (1 + x / tau) ** (-b)
def f_expc(x, tau, c): return c + (1 - c) * np.exp(-x / tau)

MODELS = {  # name: (function, initial guess, bounds)
    "linear": (f_lin, [0.1], ([-10], [10])),
    "exponential": (f_exp, [5.0], ([1e-3], [1e4])),
    "power": (f_pow, [0.5, 0.5], ([1e-4, 1e-4], [1e4, 50])),
    "exp+asymptote": (f_expc, [0.5, 0.5], ([1e-3, -20], [1e4, 1.0])),
}


def fit_models(x, y):
    """Least-squares fit of each candidate; returns {model: (params, rss, AICc)}. x in units of stages."""
    out, n = {}, len(x)
    for name, (f, p0, bounds) in MODELS.items():
        try:
            with warnings.catch_warnings():
                warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
                p, _ = curve_fit(f, x, y, p0=p0, bounds=bounds, maxfev=20000)
            rss = float(np.sum((y - f(x, *p)) ** 2))
        except Exception:
            p, rss = [np.nan] * len(p0), np.inf
        k = len(p0) + 1  # + residual variance
        aicc = n * np.log(max(rss, 1e-12) / n) + 2 * k + 2 * k * (k + 1) / max(n - k - 1, 1)
        out[name] = (list(map(float, p)), rss, float(aicc))
    return out


def h1_shape(df, tag, measure="R_loss"):
    res = {}
    d = df[df[measure].notna()]
    # (a) grand-mean and category-mean curves from position-1 trajectories (full 5-stage lag range,
    #     interfering tasks balanced by the Williams design)
    p1 = d[d.position == 1]
    curves = {"all tasks": p1, "reasoning": p1[p1.category == "reasoning"], "pattern": p1[p1.category == "pattern"]}
    curves.update({t: p1[p1.task == t] for t in TASKS})
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.3))
    for name, sub in curves.items():
        m = sub.groupby("lag")[measure].mean()
        x, y = m.index.values, m.values
        if len(x) < 5:  # no (or too few) position-1 trajectories for this subset
            continue
        fits = fit_models(x, y)
        best = min(fits, key=lambda k: fits[k][2])
        res[name] = {"n_traj": int(sub.groupby(["run", "task"]).ngroups), "n_points": len(x), "best": best,
                     "aicc": {k: v[2] for k, v in fits.items()}, "params": {k: v[0] for k, v in fits.items()},
                     "rmse": {k: float(np.sqrt(v[1] / len(x))) for k, v in fits.items()},
                     "r2": {k: float(1 - v[1] / np.sum((y - y.mean()) ** 2)) for k, v in fits.items()}}
        if name in ("all tasks", "reasoning", "pattern"):
            ax = axes[["all tasks", "reasoning", "pattern"].index(name)]
            ax.plot(x, y, "k.", ms=5, label="mean retention (position-1 tasks)")
            xs = np.linspace(0, x.max(), 300)
            for k, ls in zip(MODELS, ["--", "-.", "-", ":"]):
                ax.plot(xs, MODELS[k][0](xs, *fits[k][0]), ls, lw=1.6,
                        label=f"{k} (dAICc={fits[k][2] - fits[best][2]:.1f})")
            ax.set_title(f"{name} (n={res[name]['n_traj']} trajectories)")
            ax.set_xlabel("subsequent tasks trained (lag, in 250-step stages)")
            ax.set_ylabel(f"retention ({measure})")
            ax.axhline(0, color="gray", lw=0.5)
            ax.legend(fontsize=7.5)
    fig.suptitle(f"[{tag}] H1: shape of the forgetting curve ({measure}; 1 = just learned, 0 = zero-shot level)")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(f"figures/{tag}_h1_shape_{measure}.png", dpi=140)
    plt.close(fig)

    # (b) individual trajectories with >= 3 stages of lag: which model wins?
    wins, rows = {k: 0 for k in MODELS}, []
    for (run, task), sub in d[d.position <= 3].groupby(["run", "task"]):
        sub = sub.sort_values("lag")
        if len(sub) < 5:
            continue
        fits = fit_models(sub.lag.values, sub[measure].values)
        best = min(fits, key=lambda k: fits[k][2])
        wins[best] += 1
        rows.append({"run": run, "task": task, "category": CATEGORY[task], "best": best,
                     **{f"aicc_{k}": v[2] for k, v in fits.items()}})
    tr = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    res["per_trajectory_wins"] = wins
    res["per_trajectory_wins_by_category"] = (tr.groupby(["category", "best"]).size().unstack(fill_value=0).to_dict("index")
                                              if len(tr) else {})
    res["per_trajectory_nonmonotone_share"] = None

    # (c) how "step-like" is forgetting? share of each stage's loss change that happens in the first 25 / 50 steps
    spt = int(round(d.t[d.lag == 1].iloc[0])) if (d.lag == 1).any() else 250
    onset = []
    for (run, task), sub in d.groupby(["run", "task"]):
        s = sub.set_index("t")["loss"]
        for k in range(0, int(sub.lag.max())):
            a, b = k * spt, (k + 1) * spt
            if b in s.index and a + 25 in s.index and a + 50 in s.index and abs(s[b] - s[a]) > 0.02:
                onset.append({"run": run, "task": task, "stage_lag": k + 1, "delta_stage": s[b] - s[a],
                              "share_25": (s[a + 25] - s[a]) / (s[b] - s[a]), "share_50": (s[a + 50] - s[a]) / (s[b] - s[a]),
                              "max_within": s[[i for i in s.index if a < i <= b]].max() - s[a]})
    on = pd.DataFrame(onset)
    if len(on):
        up = on[on.delta_stage > 0.02]
        res["stage_onset"] = {"n_stage_transitions_with_loss_increase": int(len(up)),
                              "median_share_of_stage_forgetting_in_first_25_steps": float(up.share_25.median()),
                              "median_share_in_first_50_steps": float(up.share_50.median()),
                              "uniform_expectation_25": 25 / spt, "uniform_expectation_50": 50 / spt}
    # monotonicity: share of stage-to-stage transitions in which the old task's loss went DOWN (recovery)
    se = d[(d.t % spt == 0)].sort_values(["run", "task", "t"])
    se = se.assign(prev=se.groupby(["run", "task"])["loss"].shift(1))
    tr2 = se[se.prev.notna()]
    res["share_of_stage_transitions_with_recovery"] = float((tr2.loss < tr2.prev - 0.01).mean()) if len(tr2) else None
    res.pop("per_trajectory_nonmonotone_share")
    return res


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- H2: domain ratio
def category_ratio(cells, col):
    """Reasoning/pattern ratio of forgetting (1 - retention), tasks weighted equally within category."""
    per_task = (1 - cells.groupby("task")[col].mean()) if col != "abs_drop" else cells.groupby("task")[col].mean()
    r = np.mean([per_task[t] for t in TASKS if CATEGORY[t] == "reasoning" and t in per_task.index and not np.isnan(per_task[t])])
    p = np.mean([per_task[t] for t in TASKS if CATEGORY[t] == "pattern" and t in per_task.index and not np.isnan(per_task[t])])
    return r, p


def h2_domain(df, tag):
    spt = df.t[df.lag == 1].iloc[0]
    cells = df[(df.t % spt == 0) & (df.lag >= 1)]  # stage-end evaluations after >= 1 subsequent task
    res = {"per_task": {}, "ratios": {}}
    runs = cells.run.unique()
    by_run = {r: cells[cells.run == r] for r in runs}
    for col in ["R_loss", "R_loss_clip", "R_gain", "R_rel", "abs_drop"]:
        r, p = category_ratio(cells, col)
        boots = []
        for _ in range(N_BOOT if len(runs) > 1 else 0):  # cluster bootstrap over runs
            b = pd.concat([by_run[x] for x in RNG.choice(runs, len(runs))])
            boots.append(category_ratio(b, col))
        boots = np.array(boots) if boots else np.zeros((0, 2))
        ratio_b = boots[:, 0] / boots[:, 1] if len(boots) else np.array([np.nan])
        diff_b = boots[:, 0] - boots[:, 1] if len(boots) else np.array([np.nan])
        res["ratios"][col] = {
            "forgetting_reasoning": float(r), "forgetting_pattern": float(p), "ratio": float(r / p) if p != 0 else None,
            "ratio_ci95": [float(np.nanpercentile(ratio_b, 2.5)), float(np.nanpercentile(ratio_b, 97.5))],
            "diff": float(r - p), "diff_ci95": [float(np.nanpercentile(diff_b, 2.5)), float(np.nanpercentile(diff_b, 97.5))],
            "boot_share_pattern_forgetting_le_0": float((boots[:, 1] <= 0).mean()) if len(boots) else None,
            "boot_share_ratio_in_3_5": float(((ratio_b >= 3) & (ratio_b <= 5)).mean()) if len(boots) else None,
            "boot_p_diff_le_0": float((diff_b <= 0).mean()) if len(boots) else None}
        # exact permutation test over which 3 of the 6 tasks are called "reasoning" (tasks = unit of generalisation)
        pt = (1 - cells.groupby("task")[col].mean()) if col != "abs_drop" else cells.groupby("task")[col].mean()
        pt = pt.reindex(TASKS)
        if pt.notna().all():
            obs = pt[[t for t in TASKS if CATEGORY[t] == "reasoning"]].mean() - pt[[t for t in TASKS if CATEGORY[t] == "pattern"]].mean()
            diffs = [pt[list(c)].mean() - pt[[t for t in TASKS if t not in c]].mean() for c in itertools.combinations(TASKS, 3)]
            res["ratios"][col]["task_permutation_p_two_sided"] = float(np.mean(np.abs(diffs) >= abs(obs) - 1e-12))
    g = cells.groupby("task")
    tab = pd.DataFrame({"category": pd.Series(CATEGORY), "zero_shot": g.metric0.mean(), "after_own_stage": g.metric_star.mean(),
                        "gain": g.gain.mean(), "mean_metric_later": g.metric.mean(), "abs_drop": g.abs_drop.mean(),
                        "forget_rel": 1 - g.R_rel.mean(), "forget_gain": 1 - g.R_gain.mean(),
                        "n_gain_excluded": g.R_gain.apply(lambda s: int(s.isna().sum())), "n_cells": g.size(),
                        "forget_loss": 1 - g.R_loss.mean(), "forget_loss_clip": 1 - g.R_loss_clip.mean(),
                        "share_cells_below_zero_shot_loss": g.R_loss.apply(lambda s: float((s < 0).mean())),
                        "forget_loss_lag1": 1 - cells[cells.lag == 1].groupby("task").R_loss.mean(),
                        "forget_loss_sd_over_cells": g.R_loss.std()}).reindex(TASKS)
    tab.to_csv(f"results/{tag}_per_task_forgetting.csv")
    res["per_task"] = json.loads(tab.to_json(orient="index"))

    # figures: retention vs lag per task (loss-based and metric-based)
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(17, 4.5))
    for ax, col, ttl in zip(axes, ["R_loss", "R_rel", "R_gain"],
                            ["loss-based retention (dense, every 25 steps)", "relative metric retention m(t)/m*",
                             "gain-normalised metric retention"]):
        dd = df[df[col].notna()]
        for t in TASKS:
            sub = dd[dd.task == t]
            if not len(sub):
                continue
            m = sub.groupby("lag")[col].agg(["mean", "sem"])
            ax.plot(m.index, m["mean"], color=COLORS[t], lw=1.8, ls="-" if CATEGORY[t] == "reasoning" else "--",
                    marker=None if col == "R_loss" else "o", ms=3, label=f"{t} ({CATEGORY[t]})")
            ax.fill_between(m.index, m["mean"] - m["sem"].fillna(0), m["mean"] + m["sem"].fillna(0), color=COLORS[t], alpha=0.12)
        ax.axhline(1, color="gray", lw=0.5); ax.axhline(0, color="gray", lw=0.5)
        ax.set_xlabel("subsequent tasks trained (lag)"); ax.set_ylabel("retention"); ax.set_title(ttl)
        if col == "R_loss":
            lo = dd.groupby(["task", "lag"])[col].mean().min()
            ax.set_ylim(max(lo - 0.3, -6), 1.3)
    axes[0].legend(fontsize=8)
    fig.suptitle(f"[{tag}] Retention by task, averaged over orders/positions (solid = reasoning, dashed = pattern; band = s.e.m.)")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(f"figures/{tag}_retention_by_task.png", dpi=140)
    plt.close(fig)
    return res


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- H3: position
def h3_position(df, tag):
    spt = df.t[df.lag == 1].iloc[0]
    cells = df[(df.t % spt == 0) & (df.lag >= 1)].copy()
    cells["loglag"] = np.log1p(cells.lag)
    res = {}
    for col in ["R_loss", "R_loss_clip", "R_rel", "R_gain"]:
        c = cells[cells[col].notna()].copy()
        c["F"] = 1 - c[col]
        out = {}
        # (a) forgetting after exactly ONE subsequent task, by position at which the task was learned
        l1 = c[c.lag == 1]
        out["lag1_forgetting_by_position"] = {int(k): float(v) for k, v in l1.groupby("position").F.mean().items()}
        rho, p = spearmanr(l1.position, l1.F)
        out["lag1_spearman_position_vs_forgetting"] = {"rho": float(rho), "p": float(p), "n": int(len(l1))}
        # task-demeaned version (removes task difficulty differences)
        dm = l1.F - l1.groupby("task").F.transform("mean")
        rho, p = spearmanr(l1.position, dm)
        out["lag1_spearman_task_demeaned"] = {"rho": float(rho), "p": float(p)}
        # (b) regression with lag and task controlled, errors clustered by run
        try:
            m = smf.ols("F ~ loglag + position + C(task)", c).fit(cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": c.run})
            out["ols_F~loglag+position+task"] = {k: {"coef": float(m.params[k]), "se": float(m.bse[k]), "p": float(m.pvalues[k]),
                                                     "ci95": [float(x) for x in m.conf_int().loc[k]]} for k in ["loglag", "position"]}
            out["ols_n"] = int(m.nobs)
        except Exception as e:
            out["ols_error"] = repr(e)
        # (c) end-of-sequence retention by position (what a practitioner sees; confounded with lag by design)
        fin = df[(df.t + df.position * spt == df.position.max() * spt) & df[col].notna()]
        out["final_retention_by_position"] = {int(k): float(v) for k, v in fin.groupby("position")[col].mean().items()}
        res[col] = out

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4.3))
    c = cells.copy(); c["F"] = 1 - c.R_loss
    for lag, sub in c.groupby("lag"):
        m = sub.groupby("position").F.agg(["mean", "sem"])
        axes[0].errorbar(m.index, m["mean"], yerr=m["sem"], marker="o", capsize=2, label=f"lag {int(lag)}")
    axes[0].set_xlabel("serial position at which the task was learned"); axes[0].set_ylabel("forgetting (1 - R_loss)")
    axes[0].set_title("Forgetting at fixed lag vs position\n(H3 predicts lines sloping down to the right)"); axes[0].legend(fontsize=8)
    for col, mk in [("R_loss", "o"), ("R_rel", "s"), ("R_gain", "^")]:
        v = res[col]["final_retention_by_position"]
        axes[1].plot(list(v), list(v.values()), marker=mk, label=col)
    axes[1].axhline(1, color="gray", lw=0.5); axes[1].axhline(0, color="gray", lw=0.5)
    axes[1].set_xlabel("serial position"); axes[1].set_ylabel("retention at end of sequence")
    axes[1].set_title("End-of-sequence retention by position\n(position and lag confounded)"); axes[1].legend(fontsize=8)
    piv = c.pivot_table(index="position", columns="lag", values="F", aggfunc="mean")
    im = axes[2].imshow(piv.values, cmap="Reds", aspect="auto", origin="lower")
    axes[2].set_xticks(range(piv.shape[1])); axes[2].set_xticklabels([int(x) for x in piv.columns])
    axes[2].set_yticks(range(piv.shape[0])); axes[2].set_yticklabels(piv.index)
    for i in range(piv.shape[0]):
        for j in range(piv.shape[1]):
            if not np.isnan(piv.values[i, j]):
                axes[2].text(j, i, f"{piv.values[i, j]:.2f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8)
    axes[2].set_xlabel("lag (subsequent tasks)"); axes[2].set_ylabel("serial position"); axes[2].set_title("Mean forgetting (1 - R_loss)")
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=axes[2])
    fig.suptitle(f"[{tag}] H3: serial-position effect")
    fig.tight_layout()
    fig.savefig(f"figures/{tag}_h3_position.png", dpi=140)
    plt.close(fig)
    return res


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- baselines, interference, errors
def baselines(runs, df, joint_runs, tag):
    seq = [r for r in runs if not r["joint"]]
    rows = {}
    for t in TASKS:
        z = [r["recs"][0]["eval"][t]["metric"] for r in seq]
        fin = [r["recs"][-1]["eval"][t]["metric"] for r in seq]
        own = df[(df.task == t) & (df.t == 0)].metric
        rows[t] = {"zero_shot": np.mean(z), "single_task_end_of_own_stage": own.mean(), "own_stage_sd": own.std(),
                   "sequential_final": np.mean(fin), "sequential_final_sd": np.std(fin, ddof=1) if len(fin) > 1 else np.nan,
                   "joint_multitask": np.mean([r["recs"][-1]["eval"][t]["metric"] for r in joint_runs]) if joint_runs else np.nan}
    tab = pd.DataFrame(rows).T
    tab.loc["MEAN"] = tab.mean()
    tab.to_csv(f"results/{tag}_baselines.csv")
    return json.loads(tab.to_json(orient="index"))


def interference_matrix(df, tag):
    """Mean change in the old task's held-out loss caused by one stage of training on each new task."""
    spt = df.t[df.lag == 1].iloc[0]
    se = df[df.t % spt == 0].sort_values(["run", "task", "t"]).copy()
    se["dloss"] = se.groupby(["run", "task"]).loss.diff()
    se["dR"] = -se.groupby(["run", "task"]).R_loss.diff()
    se = se[se.interferer.notna()]
    piv = se.pivot_table(index="task", columns="interferer", values="dR", aggfunc="mean").reindex(index=TASKS, columns=TASKS)
    piv.to_csv(f"results/{tag}_interference_matrix.csv")
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 5.2))
    v = np.nanmax(np.abs(piv.values))
    im = ax.imshow(piv.values, cmap="RdBu_r", vmin=-v, vmax=v)
    ax.set_xticks(range(6)); ax.set_xticklabels(TASKS, rotation=30); ax.set_yticks(range(6)); ax.set_yticklabels(TASKS)
    for i in range(6):
        for j in range(6):
            if not np.isnan(piv.values[i, j]):
                ax.text(j, i, f"{piv.values[i, j]:.2f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8)
    ax.set_xlabel("task being trained (interferer)"); ax.set_ylabel("previously learned task")
    ax.set_title(f"[{tag}] Forgetting caused by one stage\n(loss-based retention lost; red = forgetting, blue = recovery)")
    fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax); fig.tight_layout(); fig.savefig(f"figures/{tag}_interference_matrix.png", dpi=140); plt.close(fig)
    same = [piv.loc[a, b] for a in TASKS for b in TASKS if a != b and CATEGORY[a] == CATEGORY[b] and not np.isnan(piv.loc[a, b])]
    cross = [piv.loc[a, b] for a in TASKS for b in TASKS if CATEGORY[a] != CATEGORY[b] and not np.isnan(piv.loc[a, b])]
    return {"mean_forgetting_caused_by_interferer": {k: float(x) for k, x in piv.mean(0).items()},
            "mean_forgetting_suffered_by_task": {k: float(x) for k, x in piv.mean(1).items()},
            "same_category_pairs_mean": float(np.mean(same)), "cross_category_pairs_mean": float(np.mean(cross))}


def format_valid(task, pred, ex_prompt):
    """Does the output have the form the task asks for (regardless of correctness)?"""
    p = pred.strip()
    if task in ("gsm8k", "arith"):
        return "Answer:" in p
    if task == "logic":
        return p.lower().strip(". ") in ("true", "false", "unknown")
    if task == "emotion":
        return p.lower().strip(". ") in ("sadness", "joy", "love", "anger", "fear", "surprise")
    src = ex_prompt.split("\n\n", 1)[1]
    if task == "mt":  # invalid if (mostly) an echo of the English source or empty
        a, b = set(p.lower().split()), set(src.lower().split())
        return len(p) > 0 and len(a & b) / max(len(a), 1) < 0.6
    if task == "summ":
        return 0 < len(p) < 0.9 * len(src) and "\n" not in p
    return True


def error_analysis(runs, tag):
    """Split forgetting into 'format/interface loss' vs 'content loss' using the raw generations saved at stage ends."""
    tests = {t: [json.loads(l) for l in open(f"datasets/processed/{t}_test.jsonl")] for t in TASKS}
    rows, examples = [], []
    for r in runs:
        if r["joint"]:
            continue
        spt, order = r["cfg"]["steps_per_task"], r["cfg"]["order"]
        by_step = {x["step"]: x for x in r["recs"]}
        for pos, task in enumerate(order, 1):
            for step in range(pos * spt, len(order) * spt + 1, spt):
                e = by_step[step]["eval"][task]
                if "preds" not in e:
                    continue
                valid = np.array([format_valid(task, p, x["prompt"]) for p, x in zip(e["preds"], tests[task])])
                sc = np.array(e["scores"])
                rows.append({"run": r["name"], "task": task, "position": pos, "lag": (step - pos * spt) // spt,
                             "trained_last": order[step // spt - 1], "format_valid": valid.mean(), "metric": sc.mean(),
                             "metric_given_valid": sc[valid].mean() if valid.any() else np.nan})
                if step == len(order) * spt and pos <= 2 and len(examples) < 12:
                    examples.append({"run": r["name"], "task": task, "learned_at_position": pos, "last_task_trained": order[-1],
                                     "prompt_tail": tests[task][0]["prompt"][-160:], "reference": tests[task][0]["answer"][:160],
                                     "output_right_after_learning": by_step[pos * spt]["eval"][task]["preds"][0][:300],
                                     "output_at_end_of_sequence": e["preds"][0][:300]})
    d = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    d.to_csv(f"results/{tag}_format_analysis.csv", index=False)
    g0, g = d[d.lag == 0].groupby("task"), d[d.lag >= 1].groupby("task")
    tab = pd.DataFrame({"format_valid_just_learned": g0.format_valid.mean(), "format_valid_later": g.format_valid.mean(),
                        "metric_just_learned": g0.metric.mean(), "metric_later": g.metric.mean(),
                        "metric_given_valid_just_learned": g0.metric_given_valid.mean(),
                        "metric_given_valid_later": g.metric_given_valid.mean()}).reindex(TASKS)
    tab.to_csv(f"results/{tag}_format_vs_content.csv")
    with open(f"results/{tag}_example_outputs.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(examples, f, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    return json.loads(tab.to_json(orient="index"))


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--tag", default="main")
    ap.add_argument("--joint_tag", default="joint")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    os.makedirs("figures", exist_ok=True)
    runs = load_runs(a.tag)
    joint = load_runs(a.joint_tag)
    assert runs, f"no finished runs for tag {a.tag}"
    df = trajectories(runs)
    df.to_csv(f"results/{a.tag}_trajectories.csv", index=False)
    summary = {"tag": a.tag, "n_runs": len(runs), "runs": [r["name"] for r in runs], "n_joint_runs": len(joint),
               "model": runs[0]["cfg"]["model"],
               "run_minutes_mean": float(np.mean([json.loads(open(f'results/runs/{r["name"]}.jsonl').readlines()[-1])["train_eval_seconds"] for r in runs]) / 60),
               "baselines": baselines(runs, df, joint, a.tag),
               "H1_shape_loss": h1_shape(df, a.tag, "R_loss"),
               "H1_shape_rel_metric": h1_shape(df, a.tag, "R_rel"),
               "H2_domain": h2_domain(df, a.tag),
               "H3_position": h3_position(df, a.tag),
               "interference": interference_matrix(df, a.tag),
               "format_vs_content": error_analysis(runs, a.tag)}
    with open(f"results/summary_{a.tag}.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(summary, f, indent=1)
    print(json.dumps({k: summary[k] for k in ["n_runs", "baselines", "H2_domain", "H3_position"]}, indent=1)[:6000])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Analysis for the Forgetting Tax study (pre-registered in planning.md).

Reads results/runs/{tag}_*.jsonl and writes tables (results/*.csv, results/summary_{tag}.json)
and figures (figures/*.png).

  H1  shape of the retention curve: linear vs exponential vs power law
  H2  reasoning vs pattern-matching forgetting rate (ratio, three normalisations)
  H3  serial-position effect beyond lag

Usage: python src/analyze.py --tag main
"""
import argparse
import glob
import itertools
import json
import os
